A central government ministry has invited global tenders for a multi-billion dollar national defense communications network project. You are a senior technical advisor heading the expert committee evaluating the bids. The project is highly critical for national security and has a strict execution deadline. After rigorous evaluation, your committee narrows down the selection to two firms. Firm A is a domestic infrastructure major that has submitted the lowest bid (L1). However, during background checks, your team discovers that Firm A has a past record of severe environmental violations, corporate governance failures, and ongoing investigations regarding financial irregularities in another ministry. Firm B is an international consortium with an absolute, unblemished global record of technical excellence, transparency, and high ethical compliance. However, Firm B's financial bid is 12% higher than Firm A's, which means choosing it would put an additional heavy burden on the public exchequer. The ministry bureaucrats are pushing for Firm A to minimize costs and promote domestic manufacturing under government guidelines, arguing that past corporate governance issues should not disqualify an L1 bidder. (a) What are the ethical and national security dimensions involved in choosing between the two firms? (b) As the head of the evaluation committee, what recommendation would you submit to the ministry and how would you justify it?

You are a young, idealistic officer belonging to the state police service and have been posted as the Additional Superintendent of Police in a district notorious for illegal sand mining. The illegal mining is operated by a powerful local mafia group that enjoys open political patronage from the ruling dispensation and has heavily bribed several local police officials. One night, during a surprise check, you intercept a fleet of trucks loaded with illegally mined sand. You arrest the drivers and impound the vehicles. Within an hour, you receive a call from your immediate superior, the Superintendent of Police (SP), ordering you to release the vehicles immediately and cover up the incident, claiming it was a misunderstanding. He tells you that your action has upset the higher authorities in the government and could destabilize your career. While you are processing this, the leader of the sand mining mafia visits your office. He offers you a massive monthly financial payout if you agree to turn a blind eye to their night operations. He also subtly warns you that if you refuse, you will be falsely implicated in a corruption case, face a hostile transfer to a punishment posting, and your family's safety could be compromised. (a) Analyze the options available to you in this situation. (b) Which course of action will you choose and why?

You are the head of a state-run primary school education board in an economically backward region. The state government has launched a highly publicized tech-driven initiative under which student attendance, continuous assessments, and benefits like scholarships and mid-day meals are linked strictly to a centralized biometric-based identification system. Within three months of implementation, data analysis reveals that in the poorest rural and tribal belts, student attendance has dropped by 35% and thousands of eligible children are being excluded from receiving mid-day meals and vital scholarships. Upon conducting field visits, you discover that the primary reasons are chronic internet connectivity failures, worn-out biometric sensors, and the fact that many poor children have eroded fingerprints due to hard manual labor helping their parents. The rules mandate that no benefits can be distributed without real-time biometric verification to prevent leakages and ghost allocations. School teachers are terrified of violating the digital mandate as the system automatically docks their salaries for manual entries. Parents are gradually withdrawing children from schools due to the stoppage of benefits. (a) Evaluate the ethical conflict between technological efficiency and social justice in this case. (b) What immediate short-term adjustments and long-term modifications would you propose to rectify this issue without compromising accountability?

A severe earthquake measuring 7.5 on the Richter scale has struck a densely populated hilly district of a state, causing widespread devastation. Hundreds of buildings have collapsed, major highways are blocked by massive landslides, and communication networks are completely down. You are the newly appointed District Magistrate of this district and are heading the disaster response management team. Within hours of the disaster, you receive reports that a remote subdivision, inhabited mostly by marginalized tribal communities, has suffered catastrophic damage, but rescue teams cannot reach it due to road blockages. Simultaneously, you receive an urgent call from the state capital conveying that a luxury resort in another part of the district has collapsed, trapping several high-profile foreign tourists, senior bureaucrats, and an influential politician's immediate family. The media has focused its entire attention on the luxury resort, and there is immense pressure from the top political leadership to divert all available specialized search-and-rescue teams, state helicopters, and heavy machinery to the resort immediately. Your resources are extremely limited, and diverting them to the resort means completely halting or delaying the rescue operations in the remote tribal subdivision for at least 48 hours, which will inevitably lead to a higher death toll among the villagers. (a) Discuss the ethical dilemmas involved in prioritizing rescue operations in this scenario. (b) How will you allocate your resources and manage the competing pressures under such extreme crisis conditions?

You are a senior executive heading the human resources department of a well-reputed multi-national consultancy firm. The firm prides itself on its diversity, gender equality, and progressive workplace policies. A brilliant young female consultant, who is considered a rising star in the company and is on track for a partnership, comes to you in absolute confidence. She states that during an out-of-town client engagement trip, a senior partner of the firm made unwanted sexual advances towards her and subtly hinted that her promotion to partnership would depend on her cooperation. The senior partner in question is the single largest revenue generator for the firm, commands immense respect among the board of directors, and is a close personal friend of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The consultant tells you that she has written proof in the form of text messages and emails, but she is terrified of immediate professional retaliation, character assassination, and being blacklisted in the industry if she files a formal complaint under the internal committee framework. She asks for your advice and intervention but explicitly requests that no formal investigation be initiated until she feels secure. (a) Identify the ethical conflicts in this case. (b) As the head of HR, what are your immediate responsibilities and what long-term systemic measures would you implement to resolve this situation?

A big corporate house is engaged in manufacturing industrial chemicals on a large scale. It proposes to set up the additional unit. Many states rejected its proposal due to the detrimental effect on the environment. But one state government acceded to the request and permitted the unit close to a city, brushing aside all opposition. The unit was set up 10 years ago and was functioning smoothly, adding to the growth of the region. A dynamic and high-profile officer who has a reputation of being an balanced and fair administrator is posted as District Magistrate of the rural district where the company is located. An anonymous letter reached the District Magistrate charging that the corporate unit is letting out toxic effluents into the nearby river and also injecting toxic waste into the groundwater, which has led to severe health issues like skin diseases, cancer, and neurological disorders among the residents of 20 surrounding villages. The District Magistrate ordered a preliminary inquiry, which confirmed the allegations. He confronted the Managing Director of the company, who subtly reminded the officer that the company is a major contributor to the state's economy, employs thousands of locals, and funds several welfare projects in the region. He also hinted at his close ties with high political authorities. (a) What are the ethical dilemmas faced by the District Magistrate? (b) Outline the course of action available to the District Magistrate and evaluate each option.

You are a senior officer working in the national drug regulatory authority. A highly reputable domestic pharmaceutical company has developed a new, low-cost drug for treating a rare, terminal type of pediatric cancer that kills thousands of poor children in India every year. The drug has shown extremely promising results in initial phases of clinical trials. However, during a routine compliance audit of the phase-III trial data, your team discovers that the company has committed serious procedural and ethical violations. They bypassed the strict informed consent protocols for several trial subjects from marginalized socio-economic backgrounds and suppressed data regarding mild-to-moderate long-term hepatic side effects in a small percentage of patients. The company management approaches you, admitting the procedural lapses but pleading for a cover-up or a conditional fast-track approval. They argue that stalling the drug's launch for a fresh round of trials will take at least three years, double the production cost, and result in the preventable deaths of thousands of poor children who cannot afford the highly expensive imported alternatives. (a) What are the ethical dilemmas and professional conflicts in this case? (b) As a regulatory officer, what decision would you take, and how would you justify it?

You are a dynamic young doctor who has recently been appointed as the Medical Superintendent of a large, state-run government hospital in a semi-urban district. The hospital is the only affordable healthcare facility for millions of poor patients in the region. Upon taking charge, you discover a deeply entrenched, unethical practice involving several senior doctors of your hospital. These doctors systematically neglect their duties in the government hospital, frequently skipping operations and OPD sessions, to run highly lucrative private clinics nearby. They deliberately mislead affluent or desperate patients into visiting their private clinics, charging heavy fees. Furthermore, you find that the hospital is facing an artificial shortage of vital diagnostic equipment and life-saving medicines because the administrative staff is deliberately leaking inventory to local private pharmacies for kickbacks. When you issue show-cause notices to the corrupt doctors, they unite against you. They command a powerful union and threaten to go on an indefinite strike, completely shutting down the hospital's emergency and trauma services, which will result in the immediate deaths of many critical patients. The local media and political leaders advise you to maintain the status quo, stating that fighting the doctors' union will destroy your career and jeopardize patient lives. (a) Analyze the ethical dilemma faced by the Medical Superintendent. (b) Formulate an action plan to eradicate this institutional corruption without putting patient safety at immediate risk.

You are a senior officer in the Ministry of Environment and Forests. A public sector power infrastructure company has applied for clearance to clear 500 hectares of pristine, dense biodiversity-rich forest land to construct a massive hydroelectric power dam project. The project is critical for providing electricity to a power-starved region, will boost industrial growth, and create thousands of jobs. However, the environmental impact assessment (EIA) report indicates that the dam will permanently submerge the natural habitat of several endangered wildlife species and displace over 10,000 indigenous tribal people who have lived in those forests for generations. The tribal communities are protesting intensely, stating that the forest is their spiritual and economic life-blood, and they refuse to accept any relocation package. The corporate lobby and top government authorities are putting immense pressure on you to sign off on the clearance, arguing that regional development and national economic growth cannot be held hostage to environmental concerns and localized tribal displacement. (a) Evaluate the ethical trade-offs between developmental imperatives and ecological/indigenous preservation. (b) As the clearing officer, what balanced framework would you propose to resolve this conflict?

You are heading a central government task force designed to evaluate and streamline the implementation of a flagship national rural employment and poverty alleviation program. During field audits in an economically depressed district, you discover a systematic nexus between local block-level bureaucrats, village panchayat heads, and private contractors. They are using advanced tech-loopholes to create hundreds of 'ghost beneficiaries' (fake accounts) and diverting millions of rupees meant for poor daily-wage laborers into private bank accounts. When you prepare to launch a formal criminal investigation against the corrupt network, the local member of Parliament (MP) calls you for a private meeting. He tells you that the village panchayat heads involved belong to a highly influential dominant community whose political support is absolutely vital for the survival of the state government in the upcoming assembly elections. He warns you that a major scandal at this juncture will cause massive political instability, disrupt the ongoing implementation of other welfare schemes, and could trigger caste-based violence in the district. He requests you to submit a diluted evaluation report focusing on technical glitches rather than administrative corruption, promising you a prestigious promotion to a central ministry in return. (a) Identify the ethical conflicts in this scenario. (b) What course of action will you adopt, and how will you justify it against the pressures of political stability?

You are a senior administrative officer posted as the Commissioner of a Municipal Corporation in a major metropolitan city. The city has seen a massive surge in unauthorized, illegal multistory commercial constructions on public land, heavily encroaching upon pedestrian pathways and narrowing public roads. These constructions are owned by highly influential local businessmen who have strong political connections across party lines. The local high court passes a strict, unambiguous order directing the Municipal Corporation to demolish all unauthorized commercial structures within 30 days and submit a compliance report. As you prepare for the demolition drive, a delegation of the local traders' association meets you. They argue that a sudden demolition will wipe out their livelihoods, cause massive job losses for thousands of poor workers employed in these shops, and trigger a severe local economic crisis. Simultaneously, the ruling party's local Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) calls you and strongly advises you to delay the demolition drive, suggesting that a law and order crisis could erupt. He hints that if you proceed aggressively, he will ensure your immediate transfer to an insignificant posting. (a) Discuss the ethical dilemmas faced by the Municipal Commissioner. (b) Outline a comprehensive strategy to execute the court's order while minimizing social and economic disruptions.

Supposing you are the Officer-in-Charge of a central procurement department which has invited global tenders for a highly advanced radar defense system. Your technical expert committee has evaluated the bids and shortlisted two foreign defense manufacturers, Company X and Company Y. Company X has quoted the lowest price (L1) and complies with all basic tender conditions. However, your intelligence desk provides you with a highly confidential report stating that Company X has a history of installing encrypted spyware 'backdoors' in its electronic systems, which could allow foreign intelligence agencies to access sensitive national defense communication data. Company Y is technically superior, has a pristine security record, but its bid is 15% more expensive than Company X. If you award the contract to Company X, you save millions of dollars of public money and satisfy the ministry's demand for speed. If you select Company Y, you protect national security but face allegations of financial favoritism, audit objections, and delays. (a) What are the ethical challenges and administrative conflicts in this case? (b) How would you proceed to resolve this dilemma?

You are a senior officer working in the environment impact clearing branch of a state government. A major multinational automobile manufacturer seeks clearance to set up a massive electric vehicle and battery manufacturing plant inside an industrial zone. The project represents the single largest foreign direct investment (FDI) in the state's history, promises to revitalize a stagnant local manufacturing sector, and create over 15,000 highly skilled jobs for the youth. However, during the technical evaluation of the project's waste disposal framework, your team discovers that the battery manufacturing process will generate vast quantities of highly hazardous chemical waste containing toxic lithium and cobalt compounds. The company's proposed treatment model complies with the letter of the current state environmental laws, which are outdated. However, your team points out that according to the latest international environmental research, the company's treatment model is deeply flawed and will inevitably lead to long-term heavy metal leaching into the groundwater table, destroying the drinking water sources of the entire industrial belt within ten years. The industrial department bureaucrats are putting immense pressure on you to clear the file quickly, arguing that strict enforcement of international standards outside the written domestic law will scare away the investor and destroy the state's economic prospects. (a) Discuss the ethical dimensions of enforcing unwritten higher standards versus adhering strictly to written, outdated domestic regulations. (b) What course of action will you choose to balance industrial growth with long-term ecological security?

You are a senior officer working in the national food safety standards authority. A leading domestic FMCG brand has launched a highly popular packaged supplementary health drink aimed at toddlers and school-going children. The product is marketed as an immunity booster and organic growth catalyst, and its sales have broken records. However, a routine post-market laboratory surveillance report reveals that the drink contains significantly higher levels of added synthetic sugars, chemical preservatives, and trace elements of heavy metals like lead than what is permissible under national food safety guidelines. Long-term consumption of the drink can cause childhood obesity, renal strain, and cognitive development delays. When you initiate steps to issue an immediate nationwide recall of the product and suspend the company's manufacturing license, the company's management meets you. They present an alternate laboratory report from a private commercial lab claiming the levels are within safe tolerances. They argue that a sudden public recall will wipe out their corporate reputation, cause a 40% crash in their stock price leading to heavy losses for small retail investors, and result in the closure of three manufacturing plants, laying off over 5,000 workers. They offer a large donation to a medical research foundation you head as a legacy project in exchange for a quiet, phased formula modification without a public disclosure. (a) Identify the ethical conflicts and the responsibilities of the regulator in this case. (b) Determine your action matrix to protect public health while managing economic implications.

You are leading an anti-corruption investigation unit within a major state infrastructure corporation. During a raid on a subsidiary office, your team recovers a set of highly encrypted personal hard drives belonging to a senior general manager. Upon decoding the files, you discover a detailed ledger recording massive financial kickbacks paid over five years to a network of high-level politicians and senior bureaucrats. However, along with the corruption records, you accidentally discover a set of confidential personal documents revealing that the general manager's teenage daughter is suffering from a highly critical, rare genetic condition and requires experimental medical treatment abroad, costing millions of rupees. The ledger explicitly shows that a significant portion of the bribe money was transferred directly to an international specialized research hospital to cover her treatment costs. The general manager breaks down during interrogation, admitting his guilt completely but pleading with you to delay the submission of the raw ledger to the court for 30 days until his daughter's critical surgery is completed, fearing that an immediate asset freeze and arrest will lead to the cancellation of her treatment and her certain death. (a) What are the ethical dilemmas faced by the investigative officer in balancing legal duty with human empathy? (b) Outline your response and justify your chosen path.

The scheme mandates that the cash benefit will be transferred directly to the bank account of the beneficiary upon producing a digital birth certificate and an official address registration card. During a surprise inspection of a remote rural clinic, you meet a young, severely malnourished tribal woman who has just given birth to twins. Her husband is a migrant daily-wage laborer who is currently untraceable. She has no digital identity card, no official bank account, and no fixed address proof as her community lives in temporary forest settlements. The rules strictly prohibit manual cash payments or exceptions to prevent leakages and audit objections. The medical officer informs you that without immediate money for post-natal nutrition and medicine, both the mother and the newborns are at high risk of mortality. The data entry operator refuses to process her file as the digital portal automatically rejects incomplete profile fields. (a) Discuss the conflict between institutional rules and humanitarian compassion in public administration. (b) How will you resolve this specific case, and what systemic policy changes would you advocate?

You are the District Magistrate of a highly sensitive, drought-prone district that is currently experiencing a severe water crisis. The state government has set up a centralized emergency drinking water distribution network using private water tankers to supply rural settlements. Due to the high value of water, a local political strongman, who owns a large network of private tankers and has deep criminal links, has effectively captured the distribution cycle. He is artificially diverting more than 60% of the government-subsidized water tankers to commercial construction sites and private industrial units owned by his associates, selling them for high profits. As a result, poor villagers, particularly women and marginalized communities, are forced to walk miles in extreme heat or buy drinking water at exorbitant prices. When your field team attempts to track the tankers using GPS and enforce fair distribution, the strongman's henchmen physically assault your field staff and threaten them with dire consequences. The local police force is compromised and hesitates to take firm action against the strongman due to his political clout in the ruling party. (a) Identify the core ethical and administrative challenges in this case. Edward Snowden, a computer expert and former CIA administrator, released confidential Government documents to the press about the existence of Government surveillance programmes. According to many legal experts and the US Government, his action violated the Espionage Act of 1971, which identified the leak of State secrets as an act of treason. Yet, despite the fact that he broke the law, Snowden argued that he had a moral obligation to act. He gave a justification for his "whistle blowing" by stating that he had a duty "to inform the public as to that which is done in their name and that which is done against them." According to Snowden, the Government's violation of privacy had to be exposed regardless of legality since more substantive issues of social action and public morality were involved here. Many agreed with Snowden. Few argued that he broke the law and compromised national security, for which he should be held accountable. Do you agree that Snowden's actions were ethically justified even if legally prohibited? Why or why not? Make an argument by weighing the competing values in this case.

As a senior officer entrusted with the responsibility of handling this issue, how are you going to address it?

Agriculture is badly affected by poor irrigation facilities. Frequent clashes among communities gave boost to illicit distillation. No major initiatives had taken place in the past either from the government's side or from social organizations to improve the lot of the people. Which new approach will you adopt to bring the problem under control?

As a senior officer in the Ministry, you have access to important policy decisions and upcoming big announcements such as road construction projects before they are notified in the public domain. The Ministry is about to announce a mega road project for which the drawings are already in place. Sufficient care was taken by the planners to make use of the government land with the minimum land acquisition from private parties. Compensation rate for private parties was also finalized as per government rules. Care was also taken to minimize deforestation. Once the project is announced, it is expected that there will be a huge spurt in real estate prices in and around that area. Meanwhile, the Minister concerned insists that you realign the road in such a way that it comes closer to his 20 acres farmhouse. He also suggests that he would facilitate the purchase of a big plot of land in your wife's name at the prevailing rate which is very nominal, in and around the proposed mega road project. He also tries to convince you by saying that there is no harm in it as he is buying the land legally. He even promises to supplement your savings in case you do not have sufficient funds to buy the land. However, by the act of realignment, a lot of agricultural land has to be acquired, thereby causing a considerable financial burden on the government, and also the displacement of the farmers. As if this is not enough, it will involve cutting down of a large number of trees denuding the area of its green cover. Faced with this situation, what will you do? Critically examine various conflicts of interest and explain what your responsibilities are as a public servant.

You are appointed as an officer heading the section in the Environment Pollution Control Board to ensure compliance and its follow-up. In that region, there were a large number of small and medium industries which had been granted clearance. You learnt that these industries provide employment to many migrant workers. Most of the industrial units have got environmental clearance certificates in their possession. The environmental clearance seeks to curb industries and projects that supposedly hamper the environment and living species in the region. But in practice, most of these units remain to be polluting units in several ways like air, water and soil pollution. As such, local people encountered persistent health problems. It was confirmed that a majority of the industries were violating environmental compliance. You issued notice to all the industrial units to apply for a fresh environmental clearance certificate from the competent authority. However, your action met with a hostile response from a section of the industrial units, other vested interest persons and a section of local politicians. The workers also became hostile to you as they felt that your action would lead to the closure of these industrial units, and the resultant unemployment would lead to insecurity and uncertainty in their livelihood. Many owners of the industries approached you with the plea that you should not initiate harsh action as it would compel closure of their units, causing huge financial loss and shortage of their products in the market. These would obviously add to the sufferings of the labourers and consumers alike. The labour union also sent you a representation requesting against the closure of the units. You simultaneously started receiving threats from unknown corners. You, however, received support from some of your colleagues, who advised you to act freely to ensure environmental compliance. Local NGOs also came to your support and demanded the closure of the polluting units immediately. (a) What are the options available to you under the given situation? (b) Critically examine the options listed by you. (c) What type of mechanism would you suggest to ensure environmental compliance? (d) What are the ethical dilemmas you faced in exercising your option?

Rakesh was working as a Joint Commissioner in the Transport department of a city. As part of his job profile, among others, he was entrusted with the task of overseeing the control and functioning of the City Transport Department. A case of strike by the drivers' union of the City Transport Department over the issue of compensation to a driver who died on duty while driving the bus came up before him for a decision on the matter. He gathered that the driver (deceased) was plying Bus No. 528 which passed through busy and congested roads of the city. It so happened that near an intersection on the way, there was an accident involving a middle-aged man. It was found that there was an altercation between the bus driver and the car driver. Heated arguments between them led to a fight and the bus driver gave him a blow. A lot of passersby gathered and tried to intervene but without success. Eventually, both of them were badly injured and profusely bleeding and were taken to a nearby hospital. The bus driver succumbed to his injuries and could not be saved. The middle-aged car driver's condition was also critical but after a day, he recovered and was discharged. Police had immediately come to the spot and an FIR was registered. Police investigation revealed that the quarrel was started by the bus driver and he had resorted to physical violence, with an exchange of blows between them. The City Transport Department management is considering not giving any extra compensation to the deceased driver's family. The family is very aggrieved, depressed and agitated against the discriminatory and non-sympathetic approach of the City Transport Department management. The deceased bus driver was 52 years of age, and was survived by his wife and two school/college-going daughters. He was the sole earner of the family. The City Transport Department workers' union took up this case and, finding no favourable response from management, decided to go on strike. The union's demand was two-fold: first, full extra compensation as given to other drivers who died on duty, and secondly, employment to one family member. The strike has continued for 10 days and the deadlock remains. (a) What are the options available to Rakesh to meet the above situation? (b) Critically examine each of the options identified by Rakesh. (c) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Rakesh? (d) What course of action would Rakesh adopt to diffuse the above situation?

You have done an MBA from a reputed institution three years back but could not get campus placement due to COVID-19 generated recession. However, after a lot of persuasion and a series of competitive tests including written and interview, you managed to get a job in a leading shoe company. You have aged parents who are dependent and staying with you. You also recently got married after getting this decent job. You were allotted the Inspection Section which is responsible for clearing the final product. In the first one year, you learnt your job well and were appreciated for your performance by the management. The company has been doing good business for the last five years in the domestic market and this year it decided even to export to Europe and Gulf countries. However, one large consignment to Europe was rejected by their Inspecting Team due to certain poor quality issues and was sent back. The top management ordered that the said consignment be cleared for the domestic market. As part of the Inspecting Team, you observed the glaring poor quality and brought it to the knowledge of the Team Commander. However, the top management advised all the members of the team to overlook these defects as the management cannot bear such a huge loss. The rest of the team members, except you, promptly signed and cleared the consignment for the domestic market, overlooking glaring defects. You again brought to the knowledge of the Team Commander that such a consignment, if cleared even for the domestic market, will tarnish the image and reputation of the company and will be counter-productive in the long run. However, you were further advised by the top management that if you do not clear the consignment, the company will not hesitate to terminate your services citing certain innocuous reasons. (a) Under the given conditions, what are the options available to you as a member of the Inspecting Team? (b) Critically evaluate each of the options listed by you. (c) What option would you adopt and why? (d) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by you? (e) What can be the consequences of overlooking the observations raised by the Inspecting Team?

The Supreme Court has banned mining in the Aravalli Hills to stop degradation of the forest cover and to maintain ecological balance. However, stone mining is still prevalent in the border district of the affected State with the connivance of certain corrupt forest officials and politicians. A young and dynamic SP who was recently posted in the affected district promised himself to stop this menace. In one of his surprise checks with his team, he found a loaded truck with stone trying to escape the mining area. He tried to stop the truck but the truck driver ran over the police officer, killing him on the spot, and thereafter managed to flee. Police filed an FIR but no breakthrough was achieved in the case for almost three months. Ashok, an Investigative Journalist working with a leading TV channel, suo moto started investigating the case. Within one month, Ashok got a breakthrough by interacting with local people, the stone mining mafia and government officials. He prepared his investigative story and presented it to the CMD of the TV channel. He exposed in his investigative report the complete nexus of the stone mafia working with the blessing of corrupt police and civil officials and politicians. The politician involved in the mafia was none other than the local MLA who was considered very close to the Chief Minister. After going through the investigative report, the CMD advised Ashok to drop the idea of making the story public through electronic media. He informed him that the local MLA was not only a relative of the owner of the TV channel but also had unofficially a 20 percent share in the channel. The CMD further informed Ashok that his further promotion and hike in pay would be taken care of, and in addition the soft loan of Rs. 10 lakhs which he had taken from the TV channel for his son's chronic disease would be suitably adjusted if he handed over the investigative report to him. (a) What are the options available to Ashok to cope up with the situation? (b) Critically evaluate/examine each of the options identified by Ashok. (c) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Ashok? (d) Which of the options, do you think, would be the most appropriate for Ashok to adopt and why? (e) In the above scenario, what type of training would you suggest for police officers posted to such districts where stone mining illegal activities are rampant?

Ramesh is a State Civil Services Officer who got the opportunity of getting posted to the capital of a border State after rendering 20 years of service. Ramesh's mother has recently been detected with cancer and has been admitted in the leading cancer hospital of the city. His two adolescent children have also got admission in one of the best public schools of the town. After settling down in his appointment as Director in the Home Department of the State, Ramesh got a confidential report through intelligence sources that illegal migrants are infiltrating the State from the neighbouring country. He decided to personally carry out a surprise check of the border posts along with his Home Department team. To his surprise, he caught red-handed two families of 12 members infiltrated with the connivance of the security personnel at the border posts. On further inquiry and investigation, it was found that after migrants from the neighbouring country infiltrate, their documentation like Aadhaar Card, Ration Card and Voter Card are also forged and they are made to settle down in a particular area of the State. Ramesh prepared a detailed and comprehensive report and submitted it to the Additional Secretary of the State. However, he was summoned by the Additional Home Secretary after a week and instructed to withdraw the report. The Additional Home Secretary informed Ramesh that the report submitted by him had not been appreciated by the higher authorities. He further cautioned him that if he fails to withdraw the confidential report, he will not only be posted out from his prestigious appointment at the State capital but his further promotion, which is due in the near future, will also get jeopardised. (a) What are the options available to Ramesh as the Director of the Home Department of the bordering State? (b) What option should Ramesh adopt and why? (c) Critically evaluate each of the options. (d) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Ramesh? (e) What policy measures would you suggest to combat the menace of infiltration of illegal migrants from the neighbouring country?

Prabhat was working as Vice President (Marketing) at Sterling Electric Ltd., a reputed multinational company. But presently the company was passing through difficult times as the sales were continuously showing a downward trend in the last two quarters. His division, which hitherto had been a major revenue contributor to the company's financial health, was now desperately trying to procure some big government order for them. But their best efforts did not yield any positive success or breakthrough. His was a professional company and his local bosses were under pressure from their London-based HO to show some positive results. In the last performance review meeting taken by the Executive Director (India Head), he was reprimanded for his poor performance. He assured them that his division is working on a special contract from the Ministry of Defence for a secret installation near Gwalior and the tender is being submitted shortly. He was under extreme pressure and deeply perturbed. What aggravated the situation further was a warning from the top that if the deal is not clinched in favour of the company, his division might have to be closed and he may have to quit his lucrative job. There was another dimension which was causing him deep mental torture and agony. This pertained to his personal precarious financial health. He was the single earner in the family with two school/college-going children and his old ailing mother. The heavy expenditure on education and medical care was causing a big strain on his monthly pay packet. Regular EMI for the housing loan taken from the bank was unavoidable and any default would render him liable for severe legal action. In the above backdrop, he was hoping for some miracle to happen. There was a sudden turn of events. His Secretary informed him that a gentleman, Subhash Verma, wanted to see him as he was interested in the position of Manager which was to be filled by him in the company. He further brought to his notice that his CV had been received through the office of the Minister of Defence. During the interview of the candidate - Subhash Verma - he found him technically sound, resourceful and an experienced marketer. He seemed well-conversant with tendering procedures and had a knack of follow-up and liaising in this regard. Prabhat felt that he was a better choice than the rest of the candidates who were recently interviewed by him in the last few days. Subhash Verma also indicated that he was in possession of copies of the bid documents that Unique Electronics Ltd. would be submitting the next day to the Defence Ministry for their tender. He offered to hand over those documents subject to his employment in the company on suitable terms and conditions. He made it clear that in the process, Sterling Electric Ltd. could outbid their rival company and get the bid and the hefty Defence Ministry order. He indicated it would be a win-win situation for both - him and the company. Prabhat was absolutely stunned. It was a mixed feeling of shock and thrill. He was uncomfortable and perspiring. If accepted, all his problems would vanish instantly and he might be rewarded for securing the much-awaited tender and thereby boosting the company's sales and financial health. He was in a fix as to the future course of action. He was wonder-struck at the guts of Subhash Verma in having surreptitiously removed his own company's papers and offering them to the rival company for a job. Being an experienced person, he examined the pros and cons of the proposal/situation and asked him to come the next day. (a) Discuss the ethical issues involved in the case. (b) Critically examine the options available to Prabhat in the above situation. (c) Which of the above would be the most appropriate for Prabhat and why?

Pawan is working as an officer in the State Government for the last ten years. As a part of routine transfer, he was posted to another department. He joined in a new office along with five other colleagues. The head of the office was a senior officer conversant with the functioning of the office. As a part of general inquiry, Pawan gathered that his senior officer carries the reputation of being a difficult and insensitive person having his own disturbed family life. Initially, all seemed to go well. However, after some time Pawan felt that the senior officer was belittling him and at times unreasonable. Whatever suggestions given or views expressed by Pawan in the meetings were summarily rejected and the senior officer would express displeasure in the presence of others. It became a pattern of boss's style of functioning to show him in bad light highlighting his shortcomings and humiliating him publicly. It became apparent that though there are no serious work-related problems/shortcomings, the senior officer was always finding one pretext or the other to scold and shout at him. The continuous harassment and public criticism of Pawan resulted in loss of confidence, self-esteem and equanimity. Pawan realized that his relations with his senior officer are becoming more toxic and due to this, he felt perpetually tensed, anxious and stressed. His mind was occupied with negativity and caused him mental torture, anguish and agony. Eventually, it badly affected his personal and family life. He was no longer joyous, happy and contented even at home. Rather without any reason he would lose his temper with his wife and other family members. The family environment was no longer pleasant and congenial. His wife who was always supportive to him also became a victim of his negativity and hostile behaviour. Due to harassment and humiliation suffered by him in the office, comfort and happiness virtually vanished from his life. Thus it damaged his physical and mental health. What are the options available with Pawan to cope with the situation? What approach should Pawan adopt for bringing peace, tranquillity and congenial environment in the office and home? As an outsider, what are your suggestions for both boss and subordinate to overcome this situation and for improving the work performance, mental and emotional hygiene? In the above scenario, what type of training would you suggest at various levels in the government offices?

Schools and colleges had shifted to alternative mode of teaching-learning-evaluation and certification. Online mode became popular during these days. India was not prepared for a sudden onslaught of such a crisis due to limited infrastructure in terms of human resource, money and other facilities needed for taking care of this situation. While carrying out a surprise inspection by the inspecting team, a minor crack was noticed in one of the piers of the elevated corridor possibly due to poor material used. You immediately informed the chief engineer and stopped further work. It was assessed by you that minimum three piers of the elevated corridor have to be demolished and reconstructed. But this process will delay the project minimum by four to six months. But the chief engineer overruled the observation of the inspecting team on the ground that it was a minor crack which will not in any way impact the strength and durability of the bridge. He ordered you to overlook the observation of the inspecting team and continue working with same speed and tempo. He informed you that the minister does not want any delay as he wants the Chief Minister to inaugurate the elevated corridor before the elections are declared. Also informed you that the contractor is a far relative of the minister and he wants him to finish the project. He also gave you a hint that your further promotion as additional chief engineer is under consideration with the ministry. What are the professional challenges likely to be faced by the project manager and his response to overcome such challenges? Parmal is a small but underdeveloped district. It has rocky terrain that is not suitable for agriculture, though some subsistence agriculture is being done on small plots of land. The area receives adequate rainfall and has an irrigation canal flowing through it. Amria, its administrative centre, is a medium sized town. It houses a large district hospital, an Industrial Training Institute and some privately owned skill training centres. It has all the facilities of a district headquarters. A trunk railway line passes approximately 50 kilometres from Amria. Its poor connectivity is a major reason for the absence of any major industry therein. The state government offers a 10 years tax holiday as an incentive to new industry. In 2010 Anil, an industrialist, decided to take benefits to set up Amria Plastic Works (APW) in Noora village, about 20 km from Amria. While the factory was being built, Anil hired the required key labour and got them trained at the skill training centres at Amria. This act of his made the key personnel very loyal to APW. APW started production in 2011 with the labour drawn fully from Noora village. The villagers were very happy to get employment near their homes and were motivated by the key personnel to meet the production targets with high quality. APW started making large profits, a sizeable portion of which was used to improve the quality of life in Noora. By 2016, Noora could boast of a greener village and a renovated village temple. Anil liaised with the local MLA to increase the frequency of the bus services to Amria. The government also opened a primary health care centre and primary school at Noora in buildings constructed by APW. APW used its CSR funds to set up women's self-help groups, subsidize primary education to the village children and procure an ambulance for use by its employees and the needy. In 2019, there was a minor fire in APW. It was quickly extinguished as fire safety protocols were in place in the factory. Investigations revealed that the factory had been using electricity in excess of its authorized capacity. This was soon rectified. The next year, due to a nationwide lockdown, the requirement of production fell for four months. Anil decided that all employees would be paid regularly. He employed them to plant trees and improve the village habitat. APW had developed a reputation of high-quality production and a motivated workforce. Critically analyse the story of APW and state the ethical issues involved. Do you consider APW as a role model for development of backward areas? Give reasons.

A new lady architect, Seema, trained at Manchester School of Architecture, UK joined as Senior Architect in your division. During the briefing about the project, Seema made some suggestions which would not only add value to the project, but would also reduce completion time. This has made the Chief Architect insecure and he is constantly worried that all the credit will go to her. Subsequently, he adopted a passive and aggressive behaviour towards her and has become disrespectful to her. Seema felt it embarrassing as the Chief Architect left no chance of humiliating her. He would very often correct her in front of other colleagues and raise his voice while speaking to her. This continuous harassment has resulted in her losing confidence and self-esteem. She felt perpetually tensed, anxious and stressed. She appeared to be in awe of him since he has had a long tenure in the office and has vast experience in the area of her work.

You are aware of her outstanding academic credentials and career record in her previous organisations. However, you fear that this harassment may result in compromising her much needed contribution in this important project and may adversely impact her emotional well-being. You have also come to know from her peers that she is contemplating tendering her resignation.

(a) What are the ethical issues involved in the above case?
(b) What are the options available to you in order to complete the project as well as to retain Seema in the organization?
(c) What would be your response to Seema's predicament? What measures would you institute to prevent such occurrences from happening in your organization?

Vinod recollects the Chairman expediting clearing of pending bills of QMR tyres.

Vinod confronts the Board Member as to why he is shying away from exposing the Chairman with the so-called solid proof he has with him. The member informs him that the Chairman refuses to yield to his threats. He adds that Vinod may earn recognition and public support if he himself exposes the Chairman. Further, he tells Vinod that once his party comes to power, Vinod's professional growth would be assured.

Vinod is aware that he may be penalized if he exposes the Chairman and may further be transferred to a distant place. He knows that the Opposition Party stands a better chance of coming to power in the forthcoming elections. However, he also realizes that the Board Member is trying to use him for his own political gains.

(a) As a conscientious civil servant, evaluate the options available to Vinod.
(b) In the light of the above case, comment upon the ethical issues that may arise due to the politicization of bureaucracy.
